Two people, P and Q, decide to independently roll two identical dice, each with 6 faces,
numbered 1 to 6. The person with the lower number wins. In case of a tie, they roll the dice
repeatedly until there is no tie. Define a trial as a throw of the dice by P and Q. Assume that
all 6 numbers on each dice are equi-probable and that all trials are independent. The
probability (rounded to 3 decimal places) that one of them wins on the third trial is _____.
questions.explaination: On rolling two fair dice independently, the probability of a tie is $P(\text{tie}) = \frac{6}{36} = \frac{1}{6}$, and the probability of someone winning (no tie) is $1 - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{5}{6}$. The game ends on the third roll if trials 1 and 2 are ties and trial 3 produces a winner: $P(\text{Trial 3}) = \left(\frac{1}{6}\right) \times \left(\frac{1}{6}\right) \times \left(\frac{5}{6}\right) = \frac{5}{216} \approx 0.0231$.

A bag contains 10 red balls and 15 blue balls. Two balls are drawn randomly without
replacement. Given that the first ball drawn is red, the probability (rounded off to 3
decimal places) that both balls drawn are red is _________
questions.explaination: Let $R_1, R_2$ be the events of drawing red balls on the first and second draws without replacement. The conditional probability that both are red given the first is red is $P(R_1 \cap R_2 \mid R_1) = P(R_2 \mid R_1)$. Given that 1 red ball is already drawn, 9 red balls remain out of $9 + 15 = 24$ total balls, so $P(R_2 \mid R_1) = \frac{9}{24} = \frac{3}{8} = 0.375$.

questions.explaination: A bijection from $A$ to $B$ implies $|A| = |B| = n$. A bijection from $A \times A$ to $A \cup B$ implies $|A \times A| = |A \cup B|$. The number of edges present in the forest generated by the DFS traversal of an
undirected graph 𝐺 with 100 vertices is 40. The number of connected components

questions.explaination: A DFS traversal of an undirected graph with $V$ vertices and $k$ connected components produces a spanning forest containing $k$ trees. A tree with $v_i$ vertices contains $v_i - 1$ edges, so the total number of tree edges in the forest is $\sum (v_i - 1) = V - k$. Given $V = 100$ and $E = 40$, we have $40 = 100 - k \implies k = 60$ connected components.

The instruction pipeline of a RISC processor has the following stages: Instruction Fetch (IF),
Instruction Decode (ID), Operand Fetch (OF), Perform Operation (PO) and Writeback (WB).
The IF, ID, OF and WB stages take 1 clock cycle each for every instruction. Consider a
sequence of 100 instructions. In the PO stage, 40 instructions take 3 clock cycles each, 35
instructions take 2 clock cycles each, and the remaining 25 instructions take 1 clock cycle
each. Assume that there are no data hazards and no control hazards.

instructions is ______.
questions.explaination: For 100 instructions in a 5-stage pipeline without branch delays, ideal cycles $= 5 + (100 - 1) = 104$. The PO stage causes pipeline stalls when operand evaluation takes extra cycles: 40 instructions require 3 cycles (2 extra cycles $\implies 40 \times 2 = 80$ stall cycles) and 35 instructions require 2 cycles (1 extra cycle $\implies 35 \times 1 = 35$ stall cycles). A processor has 16 integer registers (R0, R1, .. , R15) and 64 floating point registers (F0,
F1,… , F63). It uses a 2-byte instruction format. There are four categories of instructions:
Type-1, Type-2, Type-3, and Type-4. Type-1 category consists of four instructions, each
with 3 integer register operands (3Rs). Type-2 category consists of eight instructions, each
with 2 floating point register operands (2Fs). Type-3 category consists of fourteen
instructions, each with one integer register operand and one floating point register operand
(1R+1F). Type-4 category consists of N instructions, each with a floating point register
operand (1F).

The maximum value of N is __________.
questions.explaination: A 16-bit instruction space has $2^{16} = 65536$ encodings. Type-1: 4 instructions with $3 \times 4\text{-bit}$ registers consume $4 \times 2^{12} = 16384$. Type-2: 8 instructions with $2 \times 6\text{-bit}$ registers consume $8 \times 2^{12} = 32768$. Type-3: 14 instructions with 4-bit and 6-bit registers consume $14 \times 2^{10} = 14336$. Remaining encodings $= 65536 - (16384 + 32768 + 14336) = 2048$. Each Type-4 instruction uses one 6-bit register ($2^6 = 64$ encodings). Thus, maximum $N = 2048 / 64 = 32$.

SRC Register1

registers, and all register fields in the instructions are of equal size.

Language $L(r) = 0^* + 1^*$ contains $\epsilon$ and $0^k, 1^k$ for each length $k \in \{1..5\}$ (11 strings). Language $L(s) = 01^* + 10^*$ contains $01^{k-1}$ and $10^{k-1}$ for each length $k \in \{1..5\}$. the disk using linked allocation. In linked allocation, each data block reserves 4
bytes to store the pointer to the next data block. The link part of the last data block
contains a NULL pointer (also of 4 bytes). Suppose a file of 1M bytes needs to be
stored in the disk. Assume, 1K = 210 and 1M = 220. The amount of space in bytes

The first 16 blocks store $16 \times 65532 = 1048512$ bytes, leaving $1048576 - 1048512 = 64$ bytes stored in the 17th block. Internal fragmentation in the last block is $65532 - 64 = 65468$ bytes.

A functional dependency 𝐹:⁡𝑋→𝑌 is termed as a useful functional dependency if
and only if it satisfies all the following three conditions:
• 𝑋 is not the empty set.
• 𝑌 is not the empty set.

questions.explaination: For each attribute $A$ among the 4 attributes, there are 3 mutually exclusive choices: $A \in X$, $A \in Y$, or $A \notin (X \cup Y)$, giving $3^4 = 81$ pairs of disjoint sets $(X, Y)$. Total useful FDs $= 81 - 16 - 16 + 1 = 50$.

questions.question_text:
Suppose a message of size 15000 bytes is transmitted from a source to a destination
using IPv4 protocol via two routers as shown in the figure. Each router has a defined
maximum transmission unit (MTU) as shown in the figure, including IP header.
The number of fragments that will be delivered to the destination is ________ .
(Answer in integer)

Organising Institute: IIT Roorkee
questions.subtopic: Fragmentation and IP addressing, IPv4, CIDR notation
questions.explaination: At Router-1, max payload per fragment is $\lfloor (5000 - 20) / 8 \rfloor \times 8 = 4976$ bytes. 15000 bytes payload is fragmented into payloads of 4976, 4976, 4976, and 72 bytes (4 fragments). At Router-2 ($\text{MTU} = 3000$, max payload $\lfloor 2980/8 \rfloor \times 8 = 2976$ bytes), each of the three 4976-byte fragments splits into 2 fragments ($2976 + 2000$), yielding $3 \times 2 = 6$ fragments. The 72-byte fragment passes through intact. Total delivered fragments = $6 + 1 = 7$.
